name: Cryptic crossword No 29,868
preamble: The clue for 12ac has been amended to provide the correct complement of vowels.

clue.text: Every reason you should order sex on cue!

definitions.note: a phrase standing for 'there is no excuse not to', so it fits the answer as an idiom rather than a plain synonym

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put into a new sequence

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky case for demanding sex whenever you like.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs into 'order', which reads as the verb of demanding; it is the rearranging signal for the last three words, and NO EXCUSE is the result.
explanation.definitionFit: If there is no excuse for not doing something, then every reason exists to go ahead with it; the idiom and the clue phrase mean the same.

clue.text: Clean break when book replaced by daughter

indicators.note: one thing being replaced by another means a letter is swapped out for a different one

blocks.note: to bust something is to break it
B is the abbreviation for book; this letter goes out
D is the abbreviation for daughter; this letter comes in

explanation.surface: A clean break in a family, with a daughter taking the place of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clean break' looks like one phrase but splits: 'Clean' is the definition, 'break' is BUST, whose B becomes D. The puzzle's theme is dying, and BITE (5 down) the DUST is one way to say it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dust a room is to wipe away the powdery dirt, a routine household chore and so a kind of cleaning.

clue.text: Follow the sun and be destroyed?

blocks.note: first meaning: head in the direction the sun travels across the sky
second meaning: an informal idiom for being lost, ruined or killed

explanation.surface: A traveller chasing the sunset, with a hint that the journey may end badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The sun moves across the sky towards its setting point, so following it means travelling that way; the same two-word phrase is slang for perishing, part of the puzzle's theme of dying.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun sets in that direction, and the idiom for being ruined or dying comes from the same image of the sun going down.

clue.text: One month before electronic components will be contamination-free

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming before means sitting higher, so the first parts are placed ahead of the last

blocks.note: one is a, the indefinite article
the short form of September
IC stands for integrated circuit, a common electronic component

explanation.surface: A deadline: within a month the electronics will be free of contaminants.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a factory schedule; 'One' is just the article, and 'electronic components' are integrated circuits, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sterile and free of germs that might cause infection is described with this medical word, as with surgical equipment.

clue.text: Smart but somewhat inhibited

indicators.note: somewhat means only to a degree, so just part of the next word is used

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: Someone clever but rather shy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like the adjective for clever, but it is the verb meaning to sting. The answer joins 2 down in BITE THE DUST, one of the theme's phrases for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, both describe a sharp stinging pain, like cold wind or a chilli that makes the mouth burn.

clue.text: Paying member, inferior to writer, Regina

blocks.note: sub- is the prefix for under or lower in rank
a scribe is one who writes
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen, as on British coins

explanation.surface: A list of club members ranked below a writer and the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Regina is the Latin title of the Queen, abbreviated R in royal ciphers such as ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who pays a regular fee to belong to a club, magazine or service is a member who pays.

clue.text: Caught ascending with loss of pressure to achieve take-off

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the order runs backwards
a loss means something is dropped, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: to be caught is to be trapped
P is the symbol for pressure; one of the two goes

explanation.surface: A climbing aircraft losing cabin pressure as it tries to get airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAPPED read upwards is DEPPART, which has two Ps; dropping one leaves DEPART, which also means to die, fitting the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane that takes off is leaving its airport, and leaving a place is exactly what this verb describes.

clue.text: Packed Oslo twice up for development

indicators.note: to develop is to change and grow into a new form, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
the little word repeated, as instructed

explanation.surface: Crowded Oslo has been dug up twice for new building projects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice up' is not a direction but an instruction to write the word twice, giving the letters to mix with the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A place densely full of people is crowded, and crowded means packed in the sense of filled to capacity.

clue.text: Get into a habit that is holding back career

definitions.note: the answer is transitive, to make someone used to something; the definition is loosely intransitive

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the letters run in the opposite order
to hold something is to have it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
to career is to run headlong

explanation.surface: Someone settling into routine holds back their career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' is the verb for rushing headlong, not a job, and 'that is' is the Latin abbreviation i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone accustomed to something unpleasant through repeated exposure is to habituate them, so getting used to it becomes habit.

clue.text: No longer the thing, to retire?

blocks.note: ex- means former, no longer
'it' is the thing, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: Something that has gone out of fashion might as well retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the thing' sounds like the fashionable thing, but it is just IT; the answer is also a stage direction and a euphemism for death, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave or go out, especially from a stage, is to withdraw, so the stage direction and retire share a sense.

clue.text: Means to go east of state road

indicators.note: in an across entry, east is to the right, so the first piece named is placed after

blocks.note: to state something is to express it
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: Directions for travelling east out of a state along its highways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a region of a country but is the verb to say; 'Means' is the noun way, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast multi-lane highway for through traffic, chiefly in North America, is a major kind of road.

clue.text: Pretentious sitcom character by chance catching cold in this country

indicators.note: to catch something is to take hold of it, so one piece goes inside another
being in something means sitting within it, so this unit is put inside the next

blocks.note: a bet is a chance taken on an outcome
C for cold, as on a tap
for a British setter, this country is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A snobbish sitcom figure happens to catch a cold while in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyacinth Bucket of the BBC sitcom Keeping Up Appearances insists it is pronounced 'Bouquet'. The puzzle's theme gives KICK (26 across) the BUCKET.
explanation.definitionFit: The snobbish social climber at the centre of a classic British television comedy carries this surname, which she always gives a French pronunciation.

clue.text: Handy means of felling oak with the car’s explosive power

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A lumberjack's tip: fell an oak with the explosive force of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felling' suggests cutting down trees, but the oak is only letters; what is felled is an opponent, and 'Handy' means done with the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp blow struck with the side of the hand in a martial art can knock an opponent down, so it is a means of felling done by hand.

clue.text: My name is – goodness – dirt!

blocks.note: introducing yourself, 'my name is X' is the same as 'I'm X'
purity is moral goodness

explanation.surface: Someone introduces themselves, with a shocked exclamation, as Dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goodness' reads as an exclamation of surprise but is a noun for virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign matter that soils or contaminates something is filth, and filth is another word for dirt.

clue.text: Report the old man

blocks.note: first meaning: a sharp explosive sound
second meaning: an informal word for father

explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' reads as a verb about telling on someone, but it is the noun for the bang of a gun. POP one's CLOGS (27 across) is part of the dying theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the loud bang of a shot, a small burst of sound; 'the old man' is slang for one's father, often called Dad.

clue.text: Date agreed? Possibly lower

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement out of many, so these letters may be set in another order

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for date
taken as written

explanation.surface: A meeting has been fixed, though perhaps it will be lowered in priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date' gives only its abbreviation, and 'lower' is the verb to bring down, not the comparative of low.
explanation.definitionFit: To reduce someone or something in rank, status or quality is to bring it down, the verb sense of lower.

clue.text: Something spotted when one had got up, eyes opening

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means rising from the bottom, so the order is turned round
the opening of a word is its beginning, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: 'one had' contracts to I'd
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A sleeper notices something on waking, as their eyes open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' sounds like seen, but means covered in spots, as the cube used in board games is. The answer is also the plainest word in the dying theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The small cube thrown in board games is marked with one to six pips, so it is literally a thing covered in spots.

clue.text: Musician reversing taxi, grabbed by the male police officer

indicators.note: something grabbed is held in the grip of another, so it goes inside
to reverse is to go backwards, so the whole string is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
a cab is a taxi
PC is a police constable

explanation.surface: A musician backs up a taxi and is nabbed by a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' seems to apply only to the taxi, but it turns the whole of the following wordplay backwards. C. P. E. Bach was Carl Philipp Emanuel, a son of J. S. Bach.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Philipp Emanuel was a celebrated eighteenth-century German composer and keyboard player, a son of Johann Sebastian.

clue.text: Commercial produce around tree cut

blocks.note: c. is short for circa, Latin for around
the ash is a tree
to crop is to cut short

explanation.surface: A farmer's goods for market grown around a felled tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal but is the single letter from circa, used with dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop grown to be sold for profit rather than eaten by the farmer is farm produce raised for trade.

clue.text: Stand is protecting England’s earliest plants

indicators.note: the earliest part of a word is where it begins, so only its first letter is used
to protect is to shield by surrounding, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a dais is a raised platform or stand
taken as written
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A sports stand shelters England's first spring growth.
explanation.walkthrough: A stand here is a raised platform, not seating at a ground. With 23 down the answer gives PUSH UP THE DAISIES, another phrase from the theme of dying.
explanation.definitionFit: These small white-petalled flowers with yellow centres growing on lawns are common flowering plants.

clue.text: Key used in song of praise – a bugbear

indicators.note: something used in another is placed within it

blocks.note: an anthem is a song of praise
A is a musical key
taken as written

explanation.surface: A disliked key turns up in a hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'a bugbear' look like the whole definition, but the article is wordplay, supplying the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intensely disliked or detested is a pet hate, and a pet hate is what a bugbear is.

clue.text: Parvenu ancestral housing shade

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so the words hold the letters within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A social climber's ancestral home with its window blinds.
explanation.walkthrough: A parvenu is an upstart who has newly risen in society; the answer straddles the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle difference in tone, meaning or colour is a fine gradation, and shade is used for just such a slight variation.

clue.text: Paper is, however, full of decay

indicators.note: a thing full of something has it inside, so the letters lie within the words

blocks.note: the letters run across three words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: Paper, however much else it does, is prone to rotting.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma interrupts the run of letters but punctuation is ignored. The answer also means to die, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber or paper that rots and deteriorates with age is said to go bad in this way, a sense of decay.

clue.text: Hike – or gym exercise?

blocks.note: first meaning: to raise, as with prices
second meaning: pressing the body up from the floor with the arms

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hike' suggests a long walk, but here it is to increase. With 20 down it makes PUSH UP THE DAISIES, to be dead and buried.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise prices or rates sharply is to increase them, and the press-up done face down on the floor shares the same words.

clue.text: Now into April and start of Spring presidential reviews of troops?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: once April has begun, the month before it is over
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: As spring arrives in April, a president inspects parading troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now into April' is a little riddle: if it is April, the previous month is past. The question mark flags that presidents are only one example of who takes the salute.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial parades of troops filing past a saluting dignitary, such as a head of state, are formal military reviews.

clue.text: Fool around with second hand

indicators.note: to turn around is to face the other way, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: a sap is a gullible fool
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Messing about with a used watch, or second-hand goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second hand' reads as one phrase, but splits: S comes from 'second' and 'hand' is the verb definition. The answer also means to die, in the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something to someone by hand, as when passing the salt, is the verb sense of hand.

clue.text: Give up blow?

blocks.note: first meaning: to stop a habit, as in quitting smoking
second meaning: a strike delivered with the foot

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the clue reads like a single phrase about surrendering a punch, while it is two separate meanings. With 12 across it makes KICK THE BUCKET, to die.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit an addiction is informally to stop it entirely, and a strike with the foot is a forceful hit, both senses of the four-letter word.

clue.text: Klimt’s definitive work? Plonker!

blocks.note: first meaning: Gustav Klimt's famous painting, whose title has the definite article
second meaning: Chambers gives plonker as a big smacking one

explanation.surface: An art critic praises Klimt's masterpiece, then calls someone an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'definitive' means with the definite article: the painting is The Kiss. Plonker is British slang for a fool, but in older slang it also means a loud, smacking one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Klimt's golden painting of an embracing couple bears this title, and an old slang word for a resounding smacker on the lips is plonker.

clue.text: Loud footwear is tacky

definitions.note: the verb clogs means gums up, which is what something tacky does

blocks.note: first meaning: wooden-soled shoes that clatter on hard floors
second meaning: blocks up, as a sticky substance does in a pipe

explanation.surface: Noisy shoes are in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tacky' reads as tasteless, but it means sticky. POP (15 down) one's CLOGS is British slang for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden-soled shoes make a clatter on hard floors, and a sticky substance obstructs pipes or works, which is the verb sense.

clue.text: Paint bird and cat soaking up sun

indicators.note: to soak something up is to absorb it, taking it inside

blocks.note: the emu is a large flightless bird
the lion is a big cat
S is the abbreviation for sun

explanation.surface: A painting of a bird and a cat basking in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paint' looks like a verb, an instruction to paint the scene; it is the noun definition, and S goes after the first letter of LION.
explanation.definitionFit: Water-based household paint used on walls and ceilings is sold in Britain under this name.
